problem: Existing VLN methods struggle to effectively integrate visual observations with instruction details during navigation, leading to suboptimal path planning and limited success rates.
motivation: Precise cross-modal alignment between what the agent observes and what the instruction says is needed for reliable path planning. Angular and visual information are entangled in the navigation graph, and instructions contain fine-grained location and object cues that are not used dynamically.
key_idea: OIKG decouples angular and visual information while strengthening edge representations in the navigation graph, and dynamically extracts key location and object details from instructions to guide navigation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract implies that gains come from separating angular from visual features in graph reasoning and from step-wise use of fine-grained landmark and object phrases.
method: Observation-graph interaction module: decouples angular and visual information and strengthens edge representations in the navigation space (graph).
Key-detail guidance module: dynamically extracts fine-grained location and object information from the instruction and uses it to guide cross-modal alignment during navigation.
